name: Nevada

context: NV 329: The no-till standard lists wind erosion among its purposes and asks for current wind erosion prediction technology to set residue needs.
cover_rules: NV 340: Terminate cover crops by chemical, winter kill or crimping and leave as much biomass and residue on the soil surface as possible to prevent wind soil loss.
NV 340: Rule of thumb seeding rate is 1.0 to 1.3 million seeds/acre.
residue: NV 329: Maintain a minimum of 60 percent residue cover (flat) on the soil surface throughout any portions of the year when the soil is not covered by living plant canopy.
NV 345: Reduced till crop interval STIR value must be no greater than 80.
barriers: NV 603: Herbaceous wind barriers need a minimum expected height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent; spacing must not exceed 10 times barrier height.
NV 589: Cross wind trap strips are at least 15 feet wide when stubble is 1 foot or more in height, and at least 25 feet wide when less than 1 foot.
windbreak: NV 380: Field windbreak target density is 35-50% with a minimum of one row; farmstead and feedlot windbreak target is 65%.
roughening: NV 609: Begin roughening on the windward edge of the field; random roughness must give a 25 percent reduction in potential erosion rate.
grazing: NV 340: Grazing a cover crop for biomass must follow a 528 Prescribed Grazing plan, and stubble height after grazing shall be no less than 4 inches.
drought: NV 340: Where irrigation water is not guaranteed, plant a cover crop to coincide with seasonal moisture to improve establishment.
seeding: NV 550: Fall plantings are generally more successful than spring seedings; broadcast rates are normally 2x the PLS rate for drill seeding.
dunes: NV 342: Plants for sand dunes must survive burial by blowing sand and sand blasting; include sand fences or brush matting where applicable.
